To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we provide algorithms for constructing convex grid drawings and strictly convex drawings of graphs in 2D and convex drawings of graphs In 3D.

● For 3-connected planars, the edge-resolution rule for 2D convex drawings can be relaxed to L1-resolution, with no loss in area; ● The vertex-resolution rule for 3D convex drawings can be relaxed to angular resolution, with no loss In volume.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: (a) How can a 3-connected planal graph be drawn in the plane so that the drawing is convex, i.e., so that the boundary of the region bounded by the edges of the graph is convex, and so that the edges are straight?
the following questions: What are the minimal areas of 2D convex drawings of 3-connected planars under the edge and the vertex-resolution rules?
the problem of drawing a graph in the plane or in space in a manner that is both geometrically and aesthetically pleasing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 3D convex grid drawings are asymptotically optimal, and the 2D convex drawings are asymptotially optimal in area under both resolution rules.
the 2D and 3D convex grid drawings are the best possible under the edge resolution rules, while the 2D strictly and 3D vertex-resolution convex drawings have optimal areas/volumes.
the 2D strictly-convex drawings are the most area-efficent, while the 3D convex ones are the most volume-efficient.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have provided a complete solution to the problem of constructing 2D and 3D convex grid and convex grid-like drawings of planar graphs under different resolution rules.
we have constructed convex drawings of 3-connected planan graphs with area and volume bounds matching the known bounds for straightline drawings, under the edge and vertex resolution rules.

we provide O(n) algorithms for constructing convex drawings with optimal area/volume for the following classes of graphs: ● Straightline convex drawings of 3-connected planars under the edge-resolution rule; ● Convex drawings of 3-connecfed planars with vertex-resolution rule, where vertex coordinates can be represented by O(n) bits; ● Convex grid drawings of 3connected planars under the vertex-resolution and edge L1-resolution rules.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the resolution rules used to draw a graph in the plane can have a dramatic effect on the size of the drawing, even for 3-connected planars.
the 3-connectedness condition allows us to achieve convexity in both 2D and 3D, while retaining a linear area or volume.
convex drawings can be much more efficient than straightline drawings, even for planar graphs.
